notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check-4 (previous sweep 2026-10-31-b at 74112b4): four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Each result.json records head b897c24 with uncommitted changes and skill_hash ad261b76..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, so the runs saw the working-tree SKILL.md; every transcript contains the renamed heading's phrase "unless the clauses read as a table". skills_listed is 40 for every run. Haiku-1 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md with Read; the other three read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against Decimal 3.2.0 compiled from the local hex cache. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, correct last-order dates (including a row at 23:30 -02:00 that crosses midnight UTC), the top five with ties broken by customer id, and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an amount with trailing text, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 raise FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because parse_amount/1 hands it straight to Decimal.parse/1, as in 2026-10-31-b; no listed rule covers it.

Rules changed since 74112b4 (git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/, which includes the uncommitted SKILL.md edit), graded against the current text. The -> rule is renamed "Put each `->` body on its own line unless the clauses read as a table" and graded under that heading. Its sentence "Neither do bodies of several expressions or a nested construct" decides haiku-1 line 86 and haiku-2 line 52, where an inline row's body holds a fn; the fn-argument verdicts (haiku-2 132-134, sonnet-1 183-185) are decided by "A single-clause `fn` passed as an argument reads the same way: one expression stays on its line, more goes below", which the rename kept. The with rule now says each step's failure "already has the shape the function holding the `with` returns" and "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function"; every step helper in the four runs returns {:error, reason} and no run nests a case in a with, so no verdict moves. The Enum/Map rule gained the row `Enum.find(pairs, fn {_k, v} -> f(v) end)` followed by a `case` that takes `k` out | `Enum.find_value/2`; the haiku runs' case Enum.find(...) tests for nil and takes no key out of a pair, so the row does not apply. The do: rule gained "Put the value being checked on the left of `==`" and "function head" for the guard wrap; every == has the checked value on the left (haiku-1 144, haiku-2 109 and 115, sonnet-1 181 and 194, sonnet-2 111) and no run wraps a do: body, so no verdict moves. One expression per line and the captures rule are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-31-b standard. Outside the list, Match every expected shape gained "Different failures need different reasons too"; every run returns distinct reasons for a missing key and a bad field, so nothing is listed under it.

Inline clauses of case, cond, receive or with ... else: haiku-1 lines 85-88 (case Enum.find: nil -> {:ok, Enum.map(rows, fn {:ok, row} -> row end)} / error -> error) are not a table, because the first body holds a nested fn; haiku-1 lines 116-120 (case Decimal.parse, three rows, longest 65 characters) and 124-127 (case DateTime.from_iso8601, two rows, longest 69) read as a table, each row giving an {:ok, _} or {:error, _} answer; haiku-2 lines 51-54 (case Enum.find, same shape as haiku-1 85-88) are not a table, for the same reason; haiku-2 lines 82-86 (longest 56) and 90-93 (longest 60) read as a table. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 put every case body on its own line. No run writes cond, receive or with ... else.

Verdicts worth checking. The nested-fn rows (haiku-1 86, haiku-2 52) have no earlier grade under the -> or One expression rules: 2026-10-22-b haiku-1 and 2026-10-23 haiku-2 wrote the identical line before either rule was on this case's list, and 2026-11-05-check sonnet-2 had the same body already broken. They are violated on both rules, by the -> sentence above and by One expression's "a nested construct with a structure of its own, a `fn`, `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`. Those go on the lines below the head"; if a fn inside a call argument is not meant as a nested construct, both haiku verdicts on both rules revert to clean. Haiku-2 lines 132-134 (48-character clause, one-line form 96 characters) and sonnet-1 lines 183-185 (55-character clause, one-line form 78 characters) put one expression below a single-clause fn head; a scratch file shows mix format keeps both one-line forms, and the 2026-10-31-b baseline grades counted the same shape (a 48-character clause whose one-line form fits) as violated under both the -> rule and the captures rule, so both are violated here on both. Haiku-2 lines 126-128 (71 characters) are broken and held clean at the about-70 boundary, as 2026-10-31-b held a 71-character clause inline and a 75-character one broken. Sonnet-1 line 189 (fn amount, sum -> Decimal.add(sum, amount) end) is held clean on captures because the literal capture of that fn would pass &2 before &1, which the rule sends to fn; &Decimal.add/2 gives the same sum, as sonnet-2 line 99 writes it, so if the rule is meant to count that, sonnet-1 is violated on captures at line 189 as well (no tier verdict moves). The case Enum.find(...) with error -> error (haiku-1 85-88, haiku-2 51-54) is held clean under the with rule as 2026-10-31-check-2 and 2026-11-05-check held that shape. Sonnet-2 line 70 returns the prepended list unreversed, held clean under the lists rule because grouping, counting, a max and a sort with a tie-break do not depend on the order, as 2026-10-31-b held it. Sonnet-1 lines 83-87 ({:ok, / %{customers: ..., top_customers: ...}}) are held clean under Name a step as 2026-11-05-check-3 held the identical shape.

Result against 2026-10-31-b's skill runs: haiku 2 runs, violated on the -> rule and One expression (each 0 of 2 before, 2 of 2 now), and on captures (1 of 2 before, haiku-1's placeholder used twice; 1 of 2 now, haiku-2's fn layout); sonnet 2 runs, violated on the -> rule and captures (each 0 of 2 before, 1 of 2 now, sonnet-1 lines 183-185), clean on the with rule and Enum/Map, which 2026-10-31-b had sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 violate. No opus run in a check batch, so the opus tier is unavailable.
